subsystems.name: Energy and hydrogen supply
subsystems.role: provides the electricity and reducing power that replace sunlight and soil.

subsystems.name: Carbon capture and fixation
subsystems.role: supplies carbon, which is almost absent as CO2 in air and must be concentrated first.
parts: electrocatalytic or catalytic reduction to formate, methanol or CO

subsystems.name: Nitrogen fixation
subsystems.role: turns inert atmospheric nitrogen into reactive ammonia for amino acids and proteins.
parts: Haber-Bosch loop or electrochemical/plasma nitrogen reduction

subsystems.name: Carbon-chain assembly
subsystems.role: builds simple molecules up into amino acids, fats, sugars and vitamins.
parts: bioreactors with hydrogen-oxidising or methanotrophic microbes

subsystems.name: Mineral nutrient loop
subsystems.role: supplies what the air cannot: phosphorus, potassium, sulfur and trace metals.
parts: mined or recovered phosphate and potash
iron, zinc, copper, magnesium and vitamin sources

subsystems.name: Food processing and formulation
subsystems.role: turns the output into safe, palatable food.

buildSteps.title: Generate the energy and hydrogen
buildSteps.detail: Electrolyse water with low-carbon electricity to make hydrogen, the reducing agent that replaces photosynthesis.

buildSteps.title: Concentrate carbon dioxide
buildSteps.detail: Pull CO2 from the air or from a concentrated waste stream and purify it, since air holds only about 0.04 percent CO2.

buildSteps.title: Make reactive nitrogen
buildSteps.detail: Fix nitrogen into ammonia, either in a conventional high-pressure Haber-Bosch loop or with an electrochemical or plasma cell running at milder conditions.

buildSteps.title: Assemble nutrients
buildSteps.detail: Feed hydrogen, CO2 and ammonia, plus oxygen and minerals, to microbes in a bioreactor, or run them through catalytic cascades, to build amino acids, fats and sugars.

buildSteps.title: Add the minerals from outside the air
buildSteps.detail: Dissolve phosphate, potassium, sulfate and trace metals from mining or recovered waste into the growth medium; these cannot come from the atmosphere.

buildSteps.title: Harvest and purify
buildSteps.detail: Separate the cells or product from the broth, break cells open if needed, reduce nucleic-acid content for food safety, and dry.

buildSteps.title: Formulate the food
buildSteps.detail: Blend with fats and micronutrients, texture the material, and test it for allergens, toxins and nutrition.

buildSteps.title: Close the loops
buildSteps.detail: Recover minerals and water from waste streams so the process depends on mining as little as possible.

prerequisites.why: the whole scheme is energy, not land, limited, so electricity price sets the cost of food.
it works in pilot plants but is far too expensive and energy-hungry to be a bulk carbon feedstock.
Haber-Bosch exists but needs high pressure and heat; electrochemical and plasma routes are still laboratory-scale.
bioreactor culture of microbes on hydrogen, CO2 and ammonia has been demonstrated and produced food ingredients.

prerequisites.tech: Phosphorus and potassium supply without mining
prerequisites.why: these elements are not in the atmosphere and must be mined or recovered from waste; no closed loop exists.

pathway.milestone: separate building blocks: green hydrogen, green ammonia, direct air capture and microbial protein in pilot plants
pathway.unlocks: proof that each nutrient can be made without farmland.

pathway.milestone: integrated biorefineries feeding CO2, hydrogen and ammonia into one bioreactor, with novel-food approvals
pathway.unlocks: food produced with no sunlight and almost no land.

pathway.milestone: recovering phosphate, potassium and sulfur from waste streams at scale
pathway.unlocks: a nutrient supply that does not depend on new mines.

pathway.milestone: fully closed nutrient synthesis costing less than conventional farming
pathway.unlocks: food decoupled from soil, weather and season — if energy stays cheap and minerals are recycled.
